```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1093/jac/dky524> (open access, PMC6419616)
* Supplementary data: individual CFU-time plots by experiment type (Figures
  S1-S4) and inoculum-stratified visual predictive checks (Figures S5-S8). The
  supplement holds no equations or parameter values.

```{r citation}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Phee_2019_colistin_fusidicAcid"))
mod_broth <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Phee_2019_colistin_broth"))
cat(mod$reference, sep = "\n")
```

Phee 2019 fits one PK/PD model to 312 static time-kill curves of six
*Acinetobacter baumannii* strains exposed to colistin and fusidic acid, alone
and in combination. The library ships the paper's two models:

* `Phee_2019_colistin_fusidicAcid` -- the final CFU model (Methods Eqs 3-8,
  Table 2). Logistic growth with a lag, a sigmoidal Emax kill per drug, an
  additive combined effect, and an empirical loss of effect over time and
  concentration that stands in for resistance development. Fusidic acid lowers
  the colistin EC50 and colistin raises the fusidic acid Emax through
  categorical (present / absent) interaction terms. Strains AB205 and AB12
  differ from the reference strains through categorical covariates.
* `Phee_2019_colistin_broth` -- the separate fit of the drug concentrations in
  bacteria-free broth (Eqs 1-2): first-order loss of colistin at 0.0175 1/h.
  Fusidic acid was stable. The final CFU model does not use this loss, because
  it did not improve the fit (P > 0.05).

The drug concentrations are static covariates (`CONC_CST_MGL`,
`CONC_FUS_MGL`, mg/L) and the observed starting inoculum
(`INOC_LOG10CFU`) sets the initial bacterial count. Each `id` in the
simulations below is one time-kill condition, not a subject.

# Population (biological context)

Six strains (Methods, Bacterial strains): the antibiotic-susceptible type
strain ATCC 19606 and five MDR clinical isolates -- OXA-23 UK clone I (AB14,
AB315), OXA-23 UK clone II (AB16), SE clone (AB12) and the colistin-resistant
AB205.

```{r strains}
strains <- data.frame(
  Strain = c("ATCC 19606", "AB14", "AB16", "AB12", "AB315", "AB205"),
  `Colistin MIC (mg/L)` = c("0.25", "0.5", "0.5", "1", "1", "> 256"),
  `Fusidic acid MIC (mg/L)` = c("128", "128", "512", "64", "256", "32"),
  `Model covariate` = c(
    "reference", "reference (model developed on AB14)", "reference",
    "STRAIN_AB12 = 1", "reference", "STRAIN_AB205 = 1"
  ),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(strains, caption = "Strains and broth microdilution MICs (Methods).")
```

Time-kill assays ran in 10 mL Iso-Sensitest broth at 37 degrees C from about
10^6 CFU/mL over 24 h, with colistin at 0.25-8192 mg/L and fusidic acid at
1-8192 mg/L. Counts below 10 CFU/mL were handled with the M3 method.

# Source trace

| Element | Source location | Value / form |
|---|---|---|
| Growth, logistic (`d/dt(cfu)` without drug) | Eq 3 | `k * cfu * (1 - cfu / cfumax)` |
| Growth rate with lag (`kg`) | Eq 4 | `-net + 2 * net * t^20 / (lag^20 + t^20)` |
| `kgrow` | Table 2 | theta_net 1.87 1/h |
| `log10bmax` | Table 2 | theta_cfumax 9.41 (log10 CFU/mL) |
| `tlag50` | Table 2 | theta_lag 0.352 h |
| Drug effect (`eff_col`, `eff_fus`, `tde`) | Eq 5 | sigmoidal Emax times `1 - beta * (1 - exp(-t * tau * C))` |
| Growth with kill | Eq 6 | `(k - E) * cfu * (1 - cfu / cfumax)` |
| Covariate form | Eq 7 | `theta * (1 + theta_cov)` |
| Combination loss of effect (`tde`) | Eq 8 | `1 - beta * (1 - exp(-t * (tau_col C_col + tau_fus C_fus + tau_comb C_col C_fus)))` |
| `ec50_col`, `emax_col`, `hill_col`, `tau_col`, `beta_col` | Table 2 | 9.86, 39.5 1/h, 0.855, 0.177, 0.895 |
| `e_ab205_ec50_col` | Table 2 | 65.2 |
| `ec50_fus`, `emax_fus`, `hill_fus`, `tau_fus` | Table 2 | 310, 23.2 1/h, 0.776, 0.0102 |
| `beta_fus` | Table 2; Methods after Eq 6 | 0.895, fixed to the colistin value |
| `e_ab205_tau_fus`, `e_ab205_beta_fus` | Table 2 | 2.12, -0.124 |
| `e_fus_ec50_col`, `e_fus_ec50_col_ab205` | Table 2 | -0.826, -0.986 |
| `e_col_emax_fus` | Table 2 | 0.579 |
| `tau_comb` | Table 2 | 1.44 |
| `beta_comb` | Table 2; Methods after Eq 6 | 0.895, fixed to the colistin value |
| `e_ab12_beta_comb` | Table 2 | -0.0523 |
| `addSd_growth`, `addSd_col`, `addSd_fus`, `addSd_comb` | Table 2 | 0.129, 2.8, 0.698, 5.14 (log10 CFU/mL) |
| Broth model, `lkdeg` | Eq 2; Results, Drug degradation experiments | log(0.0175 1/h) |

# Simulation helpers

```{r helpers}
p <- mod$theta

# One row per sampling time and condition. Each id is a time-kill condition.
make_events <- function(cond, times) {
  cond$id <- seq_len(nrow(cond))
  out <- merge(cond, data.frame(time = times), by = NULL)
  out$evid <- 0
  out$cmt <- "cfu"
  out[order(out$id, out$time), ]
}

# The model has no between-experiment variability, so rxode2 warns about a
# multi-subject solve without omega; only that message is muffled.
solve_typical <- function(model, events, ...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, events, returnType = "data.frame", ...)),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
    }
  )
}

default_cov <- function(col, fus, ab205 = 0, ab12 = 0, inoc = 6) {
  expand.grid(
    CONC_CST_MGL = col, CONC_FUS_MGL = fus,
    STRAIN_AB205 = ab205, STRAIN_AB12 = ab12, INOC_LOG10CFU = inoc
  )
}

times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 24, by = 0.25), 0.352)))
```

# Typical time-kill curves (strain AB14)

The curves below are the typical-value predictions for the reference strains
(AB14 and those sharing its parameters). They reproduce the patterns of the
paper's raw data (Figures S1-S4) and of the median lines of the Figure 2
visual predictive checks: growth to the carrying capacity by about 6 h,
colistin kill followed by regrowth by 24 h, a weak and transient fusidic acid
effect, and a sustained kill in combination.

```{r curves-ab14, fig.height = 6}
cond_ab14 <- rbind(
  data.frame(default_cov(col = c(0, 0.25, 0.5, 2, 8, 32), fus = 0), arm = "Colistin alone"),
  data.frame(default_cov(col = 0, fus = c(0, 8, 32, 128, 512)), arm = "Fusidic acid alone"),
  data.frame(default_cov(col = c(0.25, 0.5, 2), fus = c(8, 32)), arm = "Combination")
)
cond_ab14$label <- paste0("col ", cond_ab14$CONC_CST_MGL, " + fus ", cond_ab14$CONC_FUS_MGL)
sim_ab14 <- solve_typical(mod, make_events(cond_ab14, times))
sim_ab14 <- merge(sim_ab14, transform(cond_ab14, id = seq_len(nrow(cond_ab14)))[, c("id", "arm", "label")], by = "id")

ggplot(sim_ab14, aes(time, pmax(log_cfu, 0), colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dotted") +
  facet_wrap(~arm, ncol = 1) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "log10 CFU/mL (floored at 0)", colour = "mg/L",
    caption = "Dotted line: 10 CFU/mL lower limit. Compare with Figures 2 and S1-S4 of Phee 2019."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

## Strain AB205 (colistin-resistant)

```{r curves-ab205}
cond_205 <- rbind(
  data.frame(default_cov(col = c(0, 2, 8, 64), fus = 0, ab205 = 1), arm = "Colistin alone"),
  data.frame(default_cov(col = c(2, 8, 64), fus = 32, ab205 = 1), arm = "Colistin + fusidic acid 32 mg/L")
)
cond_205$label <- paste0("col ", cond_205$CONC_CST_MGL)
sim_205 <- solve_typical(mod, make_events(cond_205, times))
sim_205 <- merge(sim_205, transform(cond_205, id = seq_len(nrow(cond_205)))[, c("id", "arm", "label")], by = "id")

ggplot(sim_205, aes(time, pmax(log_cfu, 0), colour = label)) +
  geom_line() +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(x = "Time (h)", y = "log10 CFU/mL (floored at 0)", colour = "Colistin (mg/L)") +
  theme_bw()
```

AB205 grows through colistin alone up to 64 mg/L (its colistin EC50 is
`r signif(p[["ec50_col"]] * (1 + p[["e_ab205_ec50_col"]]), 3)` mg/L), and
fusidic acid restores colistin activity at the higher colistin
concentrations.

# Closed-form check of the ODE

Because the growth rate and the kill rate both multiply the same logistic
factor `cfu * (1 - cfu / bmax)` (Eq 6), the model has an exact solution for
static concentrations:
`cfu(t) = bmax / (1 + (bmax / cfu0 - 1) * exp(-G(t)))`, where `G(t)` is the
time integral of `kg(t) - E(t)`. The drug part integrates analytically,
`integral of E = E0 * ((1 - beta) * t + beta * (1 - exp(-a t)) / a)` with `a`
the sum of the `tau * C` terms; the lag part is integrated numerically. Both
sides use the same parameters, so the difference is pure solver error and the
bound is tight.

```{r closed-form}
closed_form <- function(time, col, fus, ab205 = 0, ab12 = 0, inoc = 6) {
  on_col <- as.numeric(col > 0)
  on_fus <- as.numeric(fus > 0)
  e_fus <- if (ab205 == 1) p[["e_fus_ec50_col_ab205"]] else p[["e_fus_ec50_col"]]
  ec50c <- p[["ec50_col"]] * (1 + p[["e_ab205_ec50_col"]] * ab205) * (1 + e_fus * on_fus)
  emaxf <- p[["emax_fus"]] * (1 + p[["e_col_emax_fus"]] * on_col)
  tauf <- p[["tau_fus"]] * (1 + p[["e_ab205_tau_fus"]] * ab205)
  beta <- if (on_col && on_fus) {
    p[["beta_comb"]] * (1 + p[["e_ab12_beta_comb"]] * ab12)
  } else if (on_fus) {
    p[["beta_fus"]] * (1 + p[["e_ab205_beta_fus"]] * ab205)
  } else {
    p[["beta_col"]]
  }
  e0 <- p[["emax_col"]] * col^p[["hill_col"]] / (ec50c^p[["hill_col"]] + col^p[["hill_col"]]) +
    emaxf * fus^p[["hill_fus"]] / (p[["ec50_fus"]]^p[["hill_fus"]] + fus^p[["hill_fus"]])
  a <- p[["tau_col"]] * col + tauf * fus + p[["tau_comb"]] * col * fus
  int_e <- if (a > 0) e0 * ((1 - beta) * time + beta * (1 - exp(-a * time)) / a) else 0 * time
  lagfun <- function(s) s^20 / (p[["tlag50"]]^20 + s^20)
  int_k <- -p[["kgrow"]] * time +
    2 * p[["kgrow"]] * vapply(time, function(tt) {
      if (tt == 0) 0 else integrate(lagfun, 0, tt, rel.tol = 1e-12, abs.tol = 0, subdivisions = 1000L)$value
    }, numeric(1))
  bmax <- 10^p[["log10bmax"]]
  log10(bmax / (1 + (bmax / 10^inoc - 1) * exp(-(int_k - int_e))))
}

cond_cf <- rbind(
  default_cov(col = c(0, 0.5, 2), fus = c(0, 32)),
  default_cov(col = c(2, 8), fus = c(0, 128), ab205 = 1),
  default_cov(col = 0.5, fus = 32, ab12 = 1)
)
cf_times <- c(0.1, 0.3, 0.352, 0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 12, 24)
sim_cf <- solve_typical(mod, make_events(cond_cf, cf_times), atol = 1e-12, rtol = 1e-12)
cond_cf$id <- seq_len(nrow(cond_cf))
sim_cf$closed <- unlist(lapply(cond_cf$id, function(i) {
  r <- cond_cf[i, ]
  closed_form(cf_times, r$CONC_CST_MGL, r$CONC_FUS_MGL, r$STRAIN_AB205, r$STRAIN_AB12)
}))
cf_check <- dplyr::filter(sim_cf, closed > 1)
max_abs <- max(abs(cf_check$log_cfu - cf_check$closed))
cat("Rows compared:", nrow(cf_check), " max |ODE - closed form| (log10):", signif(max_abs, 3), "\n")
stopifnot(nrow(cf_check) > 50, max_abs < 1e-3)
```

Rows below 10 CFU/mL are excluded: there the solver's absolute tolerance, not
the model, sets the error.

# Growth-model and interaction checks

```{r growth-checks}
growth <- dplyr::filter(sim_ab14, label == "col 0 + fus 0", arm == "Colistin alone")
k0 <- growth$log_cfu[growth$time == 0]
k24 <- growth$log_cfu[growth$time == 24]
cat("Drug-free: log10 CFU/mL at 0 h =", k0, "; at 24 h =", round(k24, 3), "\n")
stopifnot(
  abs(k0 - 6) < 1e-8, # starts at the inoculum
  abs(k24 - p[["log10bmax"]]) < 0.01 # reaches theta_cfumax = 9.41 by 24 h (Figure S1)
)
```

The interaction terms in Table 2 are proportional changes; the Results and
Discussion restate them as "fusidic acid reducing EC50col by 82.6%",
"colistin increasing Emaxfus by 57.9%" and AB205 being "65.2-fold" less
susceptible to colistin. The covariate-adjusted parameters the model computes
reproduce these numbers.

```{r interaction-checks}
cond_int <- rbind(
  default_cov(col = 1, fus = 0), default_cov(col = 1, fus = 1),
  default_cov(col = 1, fus = 0, ab205 = 1), default_cov(col = 1, fus = 1, ab205 = 1),
  default_cov(col = 0, fus = 1)
)
int <- solve_typical(mod, make_events(cond_int, 1))
ratio_fus_on_col <- int$ec50_col_i[2] / int$ec50_col_i[1]
ratio_col_on_fus <- int$emax_fus_i[2] / int$emax_fus_i[5]
ratio_ab205 <- int$ec50_col_i[3] / int$ec50_col_i[1]
ec50_205_fus <- int$ec50_col_i[4]
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Quantity = c(
    "Colistin EC50 with / without fusidic acid", "Fusidic acid Emax with / without colistin",
    "Colistin EC50, AB205 / reference strain", "Colistin EC50, AB205 with fusidic acid (mg/L)"
  ),
  Model = signif(c(ratio_fus_on_col, ratio_col_on_fus, ratio_ab205, ec50_205_fus), 4),
  Paper = c("1 - 0.826 (82.6% reduction)", "1 + 0.579 (57.9% increase)", "1 + 65.2", "9.86 x 66.2 x (1 - 0.986)")
))
stopifnot(
  abs(ratio_fus_on_col - (1 - 0.826)) < 1e-10,
  abs(ratio_col_on_fus - (1 + 0.579)) < 1e-10,
  abs(ratio_ab205 - (1 + 65.2)) < 1e-10,
  abs(ec50_205_fus - 9.86 * 66.2 * (1 - 0.986)) < 1e-8
)
```

# EC50 units: mg/L, not ng/mL

Table 2 prints both EC50 values in ng/mL, while the experimental concentrations
are in mg/L. If the model were fitted with concentrations in ng/mL, the
equivalent mg/L parameters would be an EC50 1000-fold lower and every `tau`
1000-fold (and `tau_comb` 10^6-fold) higher. That reading contradicts the
paper in three independent ways:

1. **Figure 2 colistin VPC.** The colistin median falls to about 6 h and then
   regrows by 24 h. Under the ng/mL reading, colistin at the MIC loses its
   transient effect within minutes and then kills steadily, with no regrowth.
2. **AB205 MIC.** AB205 has a colistin MIC above 256 mg/L. Under the mg/L
   reading its colistin EC50 is 9.86 x 66.2 = 653 mg/L; under the ng/mL
   reading, 0.65 mg/L, far below its MIC.
3. **`tau_comb`.** Under the ng/mL reading, `tau_comb * C_col * C_fus` at
   0.5 mg/L colistin and 32 mg/L fusidic acid would be 1.44 x 500 x 32000 =
   2.3e7 1/h, which removes the combination effect almost at once.

```{r ec50-units}
mod_ng <- mod |>
  rxode2::ini(
    ec50_col = 9.86 / 1000, ec50_fus = 310 / 1000,
    tau_col = 0.177 * 1000, tau_fus = 0.0102 * 1000, tau_comb = 1.44 * 1e6
  )
cond_u <- default_cov(col = 0.5, fus = 0)
u_mg <- solve_typical(mod, make_events(cond_u, c(6, 24)))
u_ng <- solve_typical(mod_ng, make_events(cond_u, c(6, 24)))
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Reading = c("mg/L (packaged)", "ng/mL (as printed)"),
  `log10 CFU/mL at 6 h` = round(c(u_mg$log_cfu[1], u_ng$log_cfu[1]), 2),
  `log10 CFU/mL at 24 h` = round(c(u_mg$log_cfu[2], u_ng$log_cfu[2]), 2),
  check.names = FALSE
), caption = "Colistin 0.5 mg/L (AB14 MIC), inoculum 10^6 CFU/mL.")
stopifnot(
  u_mg$log_cfu[2] - u_mg$log_cfu[1] > 2, # regrowth between 6 and 24 h, as in Figure 2
  u_ng$log_cfu[2] < u_ng$log_cfu[1] # no regrowth under the printed units
)
```

# Residual error: standard deviations

Table 2 lists the four residual-variability values in its "Fixed effect"
column, i.e. as THETAs, which in a NONMEM residual model are usually
standard deviations. The growth-control panel of Figure 2 gives a check:
growth-control counts are reproducible and its prediction-corrected 5th-95th
percentile band spans about 0.5 log10 (about 7000 to 22000 on the plotted
scale, read by the maintainers from the figure).

```{r residual}
band_sd <- 2 * qnorm(0.95) * p[["addSd_growth"]]
band_var <- 2 * qnorm(0.95) * sqrt(p[["addSd_growth"]])
knitr::kable(data.frame(
  Reading = c("0.129 is an SD", "0.129 is a variance"),
  `Predicted 5th-95th width (log10)` = round(c(band_sd, band_var), 2),
  check.names = FALSE
))
stopifnot(abs(band_sd - 0.5) < abs(band_var - 0.5))
```

The SD reading matches the figure. The colistin-only and combination SDs (2.8
and 5.14 log10) are large; they absorb the misfit of the empirical
resistance term across very different concentration pairs (the Discussion
notes that the stepwise fixing "may inflate unexplained variability").

## Stochastic simulation

```{r stochastic}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20190401)
cond_vpc <- rbind(
  data.frame(default_cov(col = 0, fus = 0), arm = "Growth control"),
  data.frame(default_cov(col = 0.5, fus = 0), arm = "Colistin 0.5 mg/L"),
  data.frame(default_cov(col = 0, fus = 32), arm = "Fusidic acid 32 mg/L"),
  data.frame(default_cov(col = 0.5, fus = 32), arm = "Colistin 0.5 + fusidic acid 32 mg/L")
)
nrep <- 100
cond_rep <- cond_vpc[rep(seq_len(nrow(cond_vpc)), each = nrep), ]
sim_vpc <- solve_typical(mod, make_events(cond_rep, c(0.5, 1, 2, 4, 6, 24)))
sim_vpc$arm <- rep(cond_rep$arm, each = 6)
vpc <- sim_vpc |>
  dplyr::mutate(obs = pmax(sim, 1)) |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm, time) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p05 = quantile(obs, 0.05), p50 = quantile(obs, 0.5), p95 = quantile(obs, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(vpc, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.2) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50)) +
  facet_wrap(~arm) +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Simulated log10 CFU/mL (values below 1 set to 1)",
    caption = "Median and 5th-95th percentiles of 100 simulated replicates per condition."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Broth stability model and PKNCA

The broth model reproduces the reported colistin loss. A PKNCA half-life over
0-24 h recovers `ln(2) / 0.0175` = `r round(log(2) / 0.0175, 1)` h, and 34%
of the colistin is lost by 24 h.

```{r broth}
ev_broth <- rxode2::et(amt = 4, cmt = "central") |>
  rxode2::et(seq(0, 24, by = 1)) |>
  as.data.frame()
ev_broth$id <- 1
broth <- solve_typical(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_broth), ev_broth)
broth$id <- 1 # a single-subject solve returns no id column
broth$treatment <- "colistin 4 mg/L in broth"
broth <- dplyr::filter(broth, !is.na(Cc))

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(broth, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_df <- data.frame(id = 1, time = 0, amt = 4, treatment = "colistin 4 mg/L in broth")
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 0, end = 24, cmax = TRUE, half.life = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_res <- as.data.frame(nca$result)
thalf <- nca_res$PPORRES[nca_res$PPTESTCD == "half.life"]

ref <- data.frame(
  `NCA parameter` = c("t1/2 (h)", "C(24 h) / C(0)"),
  Simulated = signif(c(thalf, broth$Cc[broth$time == 24] / 4), 4),
  Reference = signif(c(log(2) / 0.0175, exp(-0.0175 * 24)), 4),
  check.names = FALSE
)
knitr::kable(ref, caption = "Reference: Results, 'Drug degradation experiments', k = 0.0175 1/h.")
stopifnot(
  abs(thalf / (log(2) / 0.0175) - 1) < 1e-3,
  abs(broth$Cc[broth$time == 24] / 4 - exp(-0.0175 * 24)) < 1e-6
)
```

# Figure 3 (clinical probability of target attainment)

Figure 3 simulates free concentrations from a colistimethate PK model
(Karaiskos 2015, packaged as `Karaiskos_2015_colistin`) and an oral fusidic
acid PK model (Bulitta 2013, *Antimicrob Agents Chemother* 57:498-507), with
unbound fractions of 64% and 10%, through this PD model. The fusidic acid PK
model is not in the package, so Figure 3 is not reproduced here. The
packaged PD model accepts time-varying `CONC_CST_MGL` and `CONC_FUS_MGL`
for such simulations. Note that the CFU model's `t` is time since the start
of drug exposure, because the loss-of-effect term was estimated in static
24-h experiments; the paper itself did not extrapolate beyond 24 h.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **EC50 units.** Table 2 prints both EC50 values in ng/mL. The packaged
  model uses mg/L (the units of the experimental concentrations), for the
  three reasons shown in "EC50 units" above. The `tau` values are read in
  L/mg/h (`tau_comb` in L^2/mg^2/h), consistently with the same
  concentrations.
* **Carrying capacity.** Table 2 prints theta_cfumax = 9.41 "cfu/mL". The
  value is log10 CFU/mL: the logistic model runs on the linear count
  (`bmax = 10^9.41`), matching the plateau of the growth curves in Figure S1
  and population predictions down to 10^-12 CFU/mL in Figure 2.
* **Residual error.** The four residual-variability values are read as
  standard deviations of an additive error on log10 CFU/mL (see "Residual
  error" above). The residual SD is selected by experiment type: growth
  control, colistin only, fusidic acid only, or both drugs.
* **AB205 and the fusidic-acid-on-colistin EC50 term.** Table 2 reports a
  "proportional decrease in theta_EC50col with fusidic acid" (-0.826) and a
  separate one "for AB205" (-0.986). The model applies the AB205 value in
  place of the reference-strain value, as one level of a three-level
  categorical covariate (no fusidic acid / fusidic acid with a reference
  strain / fusidic acid with AB205). Stacking both terms for AB205 would make
  its colistin EC50 with fusidic acid (1.6 mg/L) lower than that of AB14
  (1.7 mg/L), whereas Figure 3 shows the combination much less effective
  against AB205 than against AB14 under the high-dose regimen.
* **Choice of beta.** Colistin alone uses theta_beta_col, fusidic acid alone
  theta_beta_fus (with the AB205 change), and both drugs theta_beta_comb
  (with the AB12 change), following Eq 8 and the Methods statement that the
  fusidic acid and combination values were fixed to the colistin estimate.
  The AB205 change in theta_beta_fus therefore applies to fusidic acid alone
  only, and the AB205 change in tau_fus applies wherever fusidic acid is
  present.
* **Initial condition.** Table 2 has no inoculum parameter; each experiment
  starts from its observed baseline, supplied as `INOC_LOG10CFU`.
* **Growth lag.** The exponent 20 in Eq 4 is a fixed constant of the
  equation. As printed, the growth rate is -theta_net before the lag time, so
  the count falls by about 0.3 log10 in the first 0.35 h.
* **Broth model residual error.** The paper does not report the residual
  error of the concentration model; `propSd` is held at zero, so the broth
  model simulates the typical profile only. Fusidic acid, which was stable,
  has no model of its own.
* **Below the limit of quantification.** The fit used the M3 method for
  counts below 10 CFU/mL; simulated values below that limit are reported as
  they are, and the plots floor them for display only. The `log10()` in the
  model has a 10^-30 CFU/mL floor that only guards against a numerically
  non-positive state.
